newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: SLOVAK FINMIN SAYS MULLS INTERNATIONAL BOND ISSUE.
newsitem.headline: SLOVAK FINMIN SAYS MULLS INTERNATIONAL BOND ISSUE.

text.p: The Slovak Finance Ministry on Monday said it was "seriously considering" issuing an unspecified tranche of bonds on international markets to help cover budget expenditures.

"Interbank money market rates show that the time now seems ripe to tap international finacial sources to help cover our budget expenditures," Marian Horvath, head of the ministry's State Assets and Liabilities Department, told Reuters. "We are now working on an analysis of foreign markets so that we could issue the bond as soon as possible, he added.

Slovak interbank money market rates with longer maturities have been hovering at around 16 to 18 percent over the past few weeks. "The (domestic) market situation makes it expensive to refinance budget expenditures, so it seems that we have to go abroad," Horvath said.
Horvath would not comment on which currency the planned bond would be denominated, nor would he say whether the issue would go through private placement or a standard auction.
"We will analyse, let's say, bonds denominated in German marks, their rates, and then we will chose a bid from foreign institution," Horvath said.
The government plans to run a budget deficit of 36.9 billion crowns this year, compared with a shortfall of 25.5 billion in 1995.
The Slovak state budget posted a deficit of 361.3 million crowns for the first two months of 1997, compared with a surplus of 2.884 billion crowns in January.
The government plans to issue 70 billion crowns worth of securities on the domestic market this year.
